text:
neel: Quick follow-up on the "window proof" idea from the RFC — I'm worried about scaling when we have many tiny tenants and the proof cache churn. thinking about proof-sharding by tenant-prefix to keep subtree sizes bounded. thoughts?

tara: makes sense. shard by hashed tenant namespace (prefix bits) so each proof-shard covers ~K tenants. then windows have multiple shard-roots + global aggregator root. that keeps single-tree work small.

dj: ACL question: do shard-roots leak cross-tenant info? we still only publish hashes, but curious about potential inference if one shard has tiny population.

neel: good point. mitigate by padding empty leaves with a canonical "zero" hash and optionally merge very small tenants into a padding bucket during digesting. privacy-first default.

maria: operationally: how do we store/serve proofs? options: 1) keep full shard trees for last N windows in a fast store (redis/rocks), 2) store only roots + index and rebuild on-demand. both have tradeoffs.

tara: hybrid looks attractive: keep hot shards in-memory for recent windows; cold shards are reconstructed from compacted per-tenant aggregates in S3 via a background job.

ops-bot: FYI deploy-visibility: prototype will add ~200 writes/sec to proof-store during peak window finalization.

dj: about verification: verifier should accept either the global root (verifies aggregator) or a shard proof (verifies tenant within shard). expose two APIs: `GET /proofs/{window}/root` and `GET /proofs/{window}/tenant/{id}`.

neel: +1. also need a canonical signature model: sign global root only, or sign each shard root? signing only global root is smallest, but verifiers need pubkey + mapping. signing each shard root increases metadata but simplifies offline verification.

tara: sign global root and include signed shard-root list inside the signed blob (signed_manifest). that way verifiers can choose shard or global verification without extra signatures.

maria: re: late arrivals: we can't keep re-signing too often or auditors will be confused. proposal: publish incremental roots with monotonically increasing root-version (v1, v2...) per window. each version is append-only and immutable. audits can reference window@version.

dj: works. we should also include a small proof of mutation: `mutations.log` per window with signed mutation-hashes so auditors can see what changed between versions.

neel: performance: building shard trees incrementally on delta-apply is cheap if we maintain per-tenant leaf-hash and update parent nodes. we should avoid full recompute. cache intermediate nodes for hot shards.

ops-bot: operation note: need eviction policy and a bounded cache size per-region to avoid OOM during big rollups.

maria: cost model: storing hot shard trees for 30 days + cold recompute cost — rough estimate: $X/day per 1M tenants (will flesh out). add telemetry to track proof-request QPS and cache-hit rate.

tara: integration with reconcile flow: during finalization we compute shard roots, produce signed_manifest, and emit `window.finalized` event that contains root-version and signed_manifest pointer. reconciler verifies and uses proofs to short-circuit expensive replay.

dj: fallback flow: if proof verification fails across regions, we fetch mismatching shard subtrees and run targeted reconciliation. worst-case full replay remains as recovery.

neel: testing plan: 1) unit tests for incremental tree updates, 2) synthetic run with tenant churn and many small tenants, 3) cross-region compare test that injects bit-flips to simulate corruption.

auditor-bot: sample CLI: `ri-proof verify --root <root> --proof-shard <json>` => returns `OK|MISMATCH|INCOMPLETE`. Also `ri-proof history --window <ts>` lists root versions and mutation hashes.

maria: decision items to add to RFC: shard size target (K), padding policy for privacy, cache retention defaults, API contract for proof retrieval, signed_manifest format, rotation/keystore plan.

tara: I'll draft the shard-sizing experiments. leaning to target ~1k-10k tenants/shard to keep proofs ~log2(K) small.

dj: I'd like a small section on backwards compatibility: existing checksum endpoints remain for 6 months, verifier libs will accept both.

neel: ok. volunteers for prototype: @maria for store + API, @tara for shard builder qps tuning, @dj for verifier CLI + tests.

maria: I'll take store + metrics.

tara: on it.

dj: will sketch CLI and test harness.

neel: thanks team. I'll update RFC with these decisions and a timeline: prototype (2 weeks), pilot (4 weeks), roll (gradual) after audits sign-off.

maria: please include a short runbook for how to handle signature key rotation and emergency root revocation.

neel: will add. :white_check_mark:
